tests.name: a Copilot-style engine gets the type's rules folder as instructionDirectories on create and resume, for chat, task try, run worker, orchestrator and fork
tests.why: fake engine records options: instructionDirectories on create for chat, task, orchestrator, worker and on resume for fork and after restart; title quotes the MUST's field and callers

tests.name: with no folder for the type, or an unknown type, nothing is passed and the view says no rules; a resume after the folder appears passes it
tests.why: no folder / unknown type pass nothing and report rules null; resume after the folder appears passes it; title quotes the MUST's cases

tests.name: a rules folder that is a link leading outside the agents folder is refused with a reason; one leading inside it is used
tests.why: rulesFor realpath check for the symlink case named in the MUST; src/host/type-rules.ts is new

tests.name: Cursor (ACP) gets the rules as one context block before the first prompt, and not again on the next turn
tests.why: fake ACP agent echoes the first prompt with the block prepended and the second without; title quotes the MUST

tests.name: the context block: a file over the cap is cut with a note, files after it are left out with a note, a non-UTF-8 file is skipped with a note
tests.why: rulesBlock cap and non-UTF-8 cases named in the MUST

tests.name: the context block: one file, several files in name order, the source named, fenced
tests.why: one and several files, fenced, source named, as the MUST's cases

tests.name: the catalog names the repository type and its rules folder, and shows the same special-repo switches as the panel, a change in either showing in the other
tests.why: browser test of the catalog's type and rules lines, switches in catalog and panel, two quick toggles, renders at three widths and two themes

tests.name: with no folder for the type, or an unknown type, nothing is passed and the view says no rules; a resume after the folder appears passes it
tests.why: checks the host view data behind the catalog (repoType and rules null, then the folder after it appears); only the data, not the catalog UI or the panel sync

tests.name: in a run, order send, change, engine-made end: the change is stored at once, shown as pending, and applied once at the turn's end
tests.why: replaces the base test that expected a 409 refusal in a running run; title quotes stored at once / applied at the turn's end

tests.name: in a run, order send, change, Stop, late events after Stop: applied exactly once and the late end changes nothing
tests.why: the Stop-then-late-events order the MUST lists

tests.name: in a run, order change, engine-made end, refused reopen: the switch stays stored, the failure is shown on it, and the next send retries
tests.why: the refusal order the MUST lists

tests.name: a run started from a session with one switch on: its orchestrator and every worker start with that switch
tests.why: orchestrator and workers carry the source session's switch; title quotes the one-switch case

tests.name: a run started from a session with no switch on, or with no source session: orchestrator and workers start with none
switches changed in the source session, or in the orchestrator, after the run started do not reach the run's later workers
tests.why: the source-changed-after-start case; snapshot stored on the run

tests: tests/unit/type-rules.test.ts::with no folder for the type, or an unknown type, nothing is passed and the view says no rules; a resume after the folder appears passes it
tests/e2e/app.spec.ts::the catalog names the repository type and its rules folder, and shows the same special-repo switches as the panel, a change in either showing in the other
findings.note: The view reports the folder found on disk, not the one the open engine got; the mapped unit test even asserts that early report, so a test expecting the passed folder until reopen would fail on head (partial: needs the right expectation, not just a base run).

tests: tests/unit/type-rules.test.ts::the context block: a file over the cap is cut with a note, files after it are left out with a note, a non-UTF-8 file is skipped with a note
findings.note: The cap test checks per-file cut notes but never the total block length; asserting the whole block stays under the cap would fail on head and expose it.

tests: tests/e2e/app.spec.ts::the catalog names the repository type and its rules folder, and shows the same special-repo switches as the panel, a change in either showing in the other
findings.note: Some acceptance renders were taken with the side panel closed; an image-inspection gap, which no fail-on-base test would expose.

tests: tests/unit/type-rules.test.ts::a Copilot-style engine gets the type's rules folder as instructionDirectories on create and resume, for chat, task try, run worker, orchestrator and fork
tests/unit/type-rules.test.ts::each type with a folder gets that folder's real path; without one, or unknown, it gets none
tests/unit/special-repos.test.ts::in a run, order change, engine-made end, refused reopen: the switch stays stored, the failure is shown on it, and the next send retries
findings.note: Missing cases (a present product-type folder, resume for task/orchestrator/worker, worker and refused-send orders in a run); the existing tests pass, so a fail-on-base check cannot reveal cases that were never written.

tests: tests/e2e/app.spec.ts::the catalog names the repository type and its rules folder, and shows the same special-repo switches as the panel, a change in either showing in the other
findings.note: Required renders not all inspected; an acceptance-evidence gap outside what a fail-on-base test checks.

notes: Head includes s2's commits (default tries, hidden New run), so actions, server, task-loop and some e2e changes belong to s2, not to these MUSTs. MUST 3's UI sync is checked only by the Playwright catalog test; the Vitest test listed covers the host view data only. Other MUST 4 order tests in special-repos.test.ts (aborted end without Stop, host restart, two quick changes) also fit. MUST 4's 'applies after this turn' label has no Vitest test (pending flag only). Review finding numbers follow the report's B-numbering; c3 matched to the rereview's partly-fixed render item.
